summary: CREATE TABLE makes a new, empty table. You list each column with its type and any rules, such as NOT NULL.
notes: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY gives each row a unique id. In SQLite it fills in 1, 2, 3 automatically if you leave it out.
DEFAULT 0 is used when an INSERT does not give a value, so DECA's dues are 0.0.
SQLite is loose about types: it will store text in an INTEGER column. Most other databases reject that, so pick types as if they were strict.
pitfall: Running the same CREATE TABLE twice gives Parse error: table clubs already exists. Use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clubs (...) in scripts you run more than once.
